17188-buccaneers-and-pirates-of-our-coas.creator: Frank R. Stockton
17188-buccaneers-and-pirates-of-our-coas.description: A book by Frank R. Stockton. Some of the West India islands, especially San Domingo, were almost overrun with wild cattle of various kinds, and this was owing to the fact that the Spaniards had killed off nearly all the natives, and so had left the interior of the islands to the herds of cattle which had increased rapidly.

8546-two-summers-in-guyenne-a-chronicle-.description: A book by Edward Harrison Barker. ough the valley with the bounding spirits of a young mountaineer descending for the first time towards the great plains where the large towns and cities lie with all their fancied wonders and untasted charm.

arxiv-1706-02698.creator: Daniel L. Lau, Yu Zhang, Kai Liu
arxiv-1706-02698.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Daniel L. Lau, Yu Zhang, Kai Liu. Structured light illumination is an active 3-D scanning technique based on projecting/capturing a set of striped patterns and measuring the warping of the patterns as they reflect off a target object’s surface.

arxiv-1806-07139.title: Using J J - K K -fold Cross Validation to Reduce Variance When Tuning NLP Models
arxiv-1806-07139.creator: Henry B. Moss, David S. Leslie, Paul Rayson
arxiv-1806-07139.description: Abstract K K -fold cross validation (CV) is a popular method for estimating the true performance of machine learning models, allowing model selection and parameter tuning. However, the very process of CV requires random partitioning of the data and so our performance estimates are in fact stochastic, with variability that can be substantial for natural language processing tasks.

arxiv-2107-10149.title: A Note On the Global Dimension of Shifted Orders
arxiv-2107-10149.creator: Özgür Esentepe
arxiv-2107-10149.description: Abstract . We consider the dominant dimension of an order over a Cohen-Macaulay ring in the category of centrally Cohen-Macaulay modules. There is a canonical tilting module in the case of positive dominant dimension and we give an upper bound on the global dimension of its endomorphism ring. 1.

arxiv-2305-17676.title: Massive white dwarfs in Rastall-Rainbow gravity
arxiv-2305-17676.creator: Wenbin Lin
arxiv-2305-17676.description: Abstract We investigate the hydrostatic equilibrium of white dwarfs within the framework of Rastall-Rainbow gravity, aiming to explore the effects of this modified gravitational theory on their properties. By employing the Chandrasekhar equation of state in conjunction with the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation, we derive the mass-radius relations for white dwarfs.

arxiv-2312-05200.title: DelucionQA : Detecting Hallucinations in Domain-specific Question Answering
arxiv-2312-05200.creator: Mobashir Sadat 1 Zhengyu Zhou 2 Lukas Lange 2 Jun Araki 2 Arsalan Gundroo 2 Bingqing Wang 2 Rakesh R Menon 3 Md Rizwan Parvez 2 Zhe Feng 2 1 Computer Science, University of Illinois Chicago 2 Bosch Research North America & Bosch Center for Artificial Intelligence (BCAI) 3 UNC Chapel-Hill msadat3@uic
arxiv-2312-05200.description: Abstract Hallucination is a well-known phenomenon in text generated by large language models (LLMs). The existence of hallucinatory responses is found in almost all application scenarios e.g., summarization, question-answering (QA) etc. For applications requiring high reliability (e.g., customer-facing assistants), the potential existence of hallucination in LLM-generated text is a critical problem.

arxiv-2312-08269.title: Quadratic Forms, K K -groups and L L -values of elliptic curves
arxiv-2312-08269.creator: Li-Tong Deng, Yong-Xiong Li and Shuai Zhai
arxiv-2312-08269.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Li-Tong Deng, Yong-Xiong Li and Shuai Zhai. Let f f be a positive definite integral quadratic form in d d variables. In the present paper, we establish a direct link between the genus representation number of f f and the order of higher even K K -groups of the ring of integers of real quadratic fields, provided f f is diagonal and d ≡ 1 ​ mod ​ 4 d\equiv 1\ \mathrm{mod}\ 4 , by applying the Siegel mass formula.

arxiv-2405-13486.title: A distinct halo population revealed from 3D non-LTE magnesium abundances
arxiv-2405-13486.creator: T. Matsuno, A. M. Amarsi, M. Carlos, P. E. Nissen
arxiv-2405-13486.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by T. Matsuno, A. M. Amarsi, M. Carlos, P. E. Nissen. Magnesium is one of the important elements in stellar physics as an electron donor and in Galactic Archaeology as a discriminator of different stellar populations. However, previous studies of Mg I and Mg II lines in metal-poor benchmark stars have flagged problems with magnesium abundances inferred from one-dimensional (1D), hydrostatic models of stellar atmospheres, both with or without the local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) approximation.

arxiv-2505-05242.title: Enhancing Treatment Effect Estimation via Active Learning: A Counterfactual Covering Perspective
arxiv-2505-05242.creator: Hechuan Wen, Tong Chen, Mingming Gong, Li Kheng Chai, Shazia Sadiq, Hongzhi Yin
arxiv-2505-05242.description: Abstract Although numerous complex algorithms for treatment effect estimation have been developed in recent years, their effectiveness remains limited when handling insufficiently labeled training sets due to the high cost of labeling the effect after treatment, e.g., expensive tumor imaging or biopsy procedures needed to evaluate treatment effects.

arxiv-2508-01063.title: Counting topological interface modes using simplicial characteristic classes
arxiv-2508-01063.creator: N. Bohlsen, I. Y. Dodin, H. Qin
arxiv-2508-01063.description: Abstract A computational approach for predicting the number of topological interface modes (TIMs) in hermitian systems using the spectral flow - monopole (SFM) correspondence is presented. The number of TIMs is determined by calculating the Chern number of a complex line bundle of local polarisation vectors over a phase space sphere surrounding a Weyl point.

arxiv-2510-24317.title: Cybersecurity AI Benchmark (CAIBench): A Meta-Benchmark for Evaluating Cybersecurity AI Agents
arxiv-2510-24317.creator: María Sanz-Gómez, Víctor Mayoral-Vilches, Francesco Balassone, Luis Javier Navarrete-Lozano, Cristóbal R. J. Veas Chavez, Maite del Mundo de Torres
arxiv-2510-24317.description: Abstract Cybersecurity spans multiple interconnected domains, complicating the development of meaningful, labor-relevant benchmarks. Existing benchmarks assess isolated skills rather than integrated performance. We find that pre-trained knowledge of cybersecurity in LLMs does not imply attack and defense abilities, revealing a gap between knowledge and capability.

arxiv-2602-10114.title: Decoupled MPPI-Based Multi-Arm Motion Planning
arxiv-2602-10114.creator: Dan Evron, Elias Goldsztejn, Ronen I. Brafman
arxiv-2602-10114.description: Abstract Recent advances in sampling-based motion planning algorithms for high DOF arms leverage GPUs to provide SOTA performance. These algorithms can be used to control multiple arms jointly, but this approach scales poorly. To address this, we extend STORM, a sampling-based model-predictive-control (MPC) motion planning algorithm, to handle multiple robots in a distributed fashion.

pmc-10522732.title: Serum concentration–guided intravenous magnesium sulfate administration for neuroprotection in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a retrospective evaluation of a 12-year single-center experience
pmc-10522732.creator: C. Wipplinger, A. Cattaneo, T. M. Wipplinger, K. Lamllari, F. Semmler, C. Geske, J. Messinger, V. Nickl, A. Beez, R.-I. Ernestus, M. Pham, T. Westermaier, J. Weiland, C. Stetter, E. Kunze
pmc-10522732.description: Delayed cerebral infarction (DCI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). The benefits of magnesium sulfate as an alternative treatment are controversial, and most previous studies examined its benefits only as adjunctive treatment to traditional nimodipine. We retrospectively analyzed aSAH patients records with magnesium sulfate between 2010 and 2021.

pmc-10762550.title: Subcentimetric papillary thyroid carcinoma with extensive lymph node and brain metastasis: case report and review of literature
pmc-10762550.creator: Andreia Amado, Elisabete Teixeira, Sule Canberk, Sofia Macedo, Bárbara Castro, Hugo Pereira, João Varanda, Susana Graça, Amélia Tavares, Carlos Soares, Maria João Oliveira, Manuel Oliveira, Paula Soares, Manuel Sobrinho Simões, Antónia Afonso Póvoa
pmc-10762550.description: SummaryWe report a 61-year-old male patient without personal history of thyroid carcinoma or radiation exposure. In 2011, he presented with a cervical mass whose biopsy diagnosed a papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) in a lymph node metastasis (LNM). Total thyroidectomy with lymphadenectomy of central and ipsilateral compartment was performed.

pmc-11046611.title: Evidence-based appraisal of the role of SJTs in selection
pmc-11046611.creator: Gurvinder Sahota, John McLachlan, Fiona Patterson, Paul Tiffin
pmc-11046611.description: A recent opinion article in Clinical Medicine promoted a new preference-based algorithm to allocate training places for the UK Foundation Programme Office (UKFPO). This replaced the previous process, which ranked candidates based on medical school academic achievement (the educational performance measure; EPM) and the score on a situational judgement test (SJT).

pmc-11461744.title: USP24 promotes autophagy-dependent ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by reducing the K48-linked ubiquitination of Beclin1
pmc-11461744.creator: Jiahui Cao, Shitao Wu, Senfeng Zhao, Libo Wang, Yahui Wu, Liming Song, Chenguang Sun, Yin Liu, Zhipu Liu, Rongtao Zhu, Ruopeng Liang, Weijie Wang, Yuling Sun
pmc-11461744.description: Ubiquitination is a post-translational modification (PTM), which is critical to maintain cell homeostasis. Ubiquitin-specific protease 24 (USP24) plays roles in various diseases, the mechanisms by which USP24 regulates hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain poorly understood. In this study, USP24 is found to be significantly downregulated in HCC.

pmc-11520164.title: Biological aging mediates the association between volatile organic compounds and cardiovascular disease
pmc-11520164.creator: Qingqing Cao, Yu Song, Changsheng Huan, Zexin Jia, Qian Gao, Xiaoqing Ma, Guihong Zhou, Siyu Chen, Jin Wei, Yuchuan Wang, Chongjian Wang, Zhenxing Mao, Jian Hou, Wenqian Huo
pmc-11520164.description: BackgroundEvidence for the relationship between individual and combined volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) is limited. Besides, the mediating role of biological aging (BA) has not been studied. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the association between VOCs and CVD risk and to explore the mediating effects of BA.

pmc-11670069.title: Cellular components of tumor microenvironment: understanding their role in lymphatic metastasis of tumors
pmc-11670069.creator: Ziyi Wang, Zehui Li, Xiangyu Sun, Wanfu Men, Yan Xu
pmc-11670069.description: Metastasis is the leading cause of cancer-related death in cancer patients. Tumor cells primarily spread through the hematogenous and lymphatic system. The underlying mechanisms of hematogenous metastasis have been well described over the past few decades. However, the understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in lymphatic metastasis is still at an early stage.

pmc-12413979.title: Allogeneic Treg-derived artificial vesicles: A promising therapeutic modality for multiple sclerosis
pmc-12413979.creator: Irina Alekseevna Ganeeva, Elvina Maratovna Gilyazova, Arthur Ajdarovich Khannanov, Mariia Eugenievna Nektorova, Alexey Michailovich Rogov, Timur Ildarovich Khaibullin, Ekaterina Anatolievna Zmievskaya, Emil Rafaelevich Bulatov
pmc-12413979.description: Introduction: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS). CD4+ CD25+hi Tregs, which normally suppress immune responses, exhibit impaired function in MS. Treg-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry immunoregulatory proteins and miRNAs that modulate T-cell activity. However, EVs from MS patients show reduced suppressive capacity, suggesting their dysfunction contributes to MS pathogenesis.

pmc-13335012.title: Mapping the “Supply–Demand–Flow” of Ecosystem Services for Ecosystem Management in China
pmc-13335012.creator: Yikun Zhang, Yadong Yang, Yongsheng Wang, Guirui Yu
pmc-13335012.description: Ecosystem services (ES) link ecosystems and human societies, yet approaches to ecosystem service flow (ESF) are constrained by ambiguous definitions and limited process‐oriented and scale‐sensitive classifications. Here, we developed a “supply–demand–flow” framework distinguishing potential and actual supply and demand, and classifying ESF into in situ, interior, and exterior flows.

pmc-13406154.title: Efficacy and Safety of Nitrous Oxide and Midazolam Sedation Protocols in Pediatric Dentistry: A Multicenter Clinical Retrospective Study
pmc-13406154.creator: Lucia Giannini, Niccolò Cenzato, Gregorio Menozzi, Alessandra Gianfiori, Gianna Dipalma, Cinzia Maspero
pmc-13406154.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Outpatient conscious sedation with titrated nitrous oxide/oxygen, alone or combined with midazolam, enabled the successful completion of all planned complex dental and minor oral surgical procedures in selected uncooperative pediatric and special needs patients.No procedure required conversion to deep intravenous sedation or general anesthesia, and no major adverse events or airway emergencies were observed.

pmc-13475062.title: How Speaker Configuration of Recorded Media Affects Subjective Ratings for Listeners With and Without Hearing Loss
pmc-13475062.creator: Todd A. Ricketts, Rebecca Krivoshey, Javier Santos-Garrido, Haiping Huang, Erin M. Picou

pmc-13583046.title: Targeting super elongation complex-driven RNA polymerase II elongation reduces plaque vulnerability
pmc-13583046.creator: Karoline E Kokot, Sebastian Reichardt, Christian Menedo, Stephan Erbe, Jasmin M Kneuer, Kaylin C A Palm, Julian Hoba, Michael Andritschke, Mirko Katzmann, Annika Reuser, Moritz von Scheidt, Michal Mokry, Junjie Xiao, Bilal N Sheikh, Nora Klöting, Ulrich Laufs, Jes-Niels Boeckel
pmc-13583046.description: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke, yet the mechanisms governing plaque stability remain incompletely understood. Endothelial activation can trigger endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, a program linked to endothelial dysfunction and lesion vulnerability. Here we investigated whether transcriptional pause release and RNA polymerase II elongation constitute an early regulatory layer that promotes endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and atherosclerosis.

pmc-13639590.title: Association of Combined Nutritional Risk and Oral Frailty Assessment with Postoperative Complications in Older Surgical Patients: A Pilot Cohort Study
pmc-13639590.creator: Hiroyasu Murata
pmc-13639590.description: Introduction:Postoperative complications are common in older adults and are influenced by frailty-related factors. This study examined whether the combined assessment of nutritional risk and oral frailty was associated with postoperative complications in older surgical patients.Methods:We retrospectively analyzed 200 patients aged ≥65 years who underwent elective surgery under general anesthesia at Kyorin University Hospital (July–October 2021).
